canonical_title: U.S. technology coalition urges policymakers to preserve open-weight AI
aliases: Open Weights and American AI Leadership
treatment: The July 24 policy letter, its principal arguments, OpenAI's later signature, and the expanded official signatory list are covered. Reinclude only for a binding U.S. policy response, a major signatory reversal or addition that changes the coalition, a formal Anthropic or Google position, or concrete legislation affecting open-weight distribution.
known_facts: NVIDIA and an initial coalition of technology companies and organizations published the July 24, 2026 letter Open Weights and American AI Leadership, urging U.S. policymakers to avoid premature broad restrictions on downloadable model weights.
The letter argues that open weights improve competition, customer control, cybersecurity defense, and sovereign deployment while acknowledging that released weights are difficult to trace or reverse.
The letter asks policymakers to expand compute access and shared training and evaluation assets, preserve a plural frontier, and distinguish legitimate distillation from unlawful extraction.

OpenAI was absent from the initial signatory list but joined later; the current NVIDIA-hosted PDF lists at least 35 organizations, including NVIDIA, Microsoft, Meta, OpenAI, Hugging Face, Mistral, Mozilla, The Linux Foundation, GitHub, Cisco, Cohere, CrowdStrike, and Palantir.
Google CEO Sundar Pichai publicly supported the message, according to Business Insider, but Google was not listed as a signatory in the current official PDF; Anthropic also remained absent.
reinclude_only_if: The U.S. government issues a binding rule, sanction, or formal policy concerning open-weight model distribution or Chinese open-weight models.
Anthropic, Google, Amazon, or another major frontier provider formally joins, rejects, or materially qualifies the coalition position.
The coalition publishes technical safety commitments, evaluation standards, or a substantially revised policy proposal.
A concrete law or enforcement action materially changes the availability or legal treatment of open-weight models.
notes: Selected on 2026-07-26 because OpenAI's later signature and expansion of the official signatory list were newly visible after the prior midday brief. The official PDF is authoritative for the current list; secondary claims that the coalition reached 50 were not used because they did not match the PDF inspected during this run.
